text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 45

An all-male panel, on its own, is weak evidence. In structural engineering women are a small minority of senior staff, so a four-man panel is roughly what chance would produce — it signals a thin pipeline more than a biased decision. It matters legally and practically only as context, not proof.

Your stronger points are concrete: a 15-vs-8-year experience gap, three led projects, and a two-week silence on a reasonable request for written reasons. "Excellent client relationships" is a legitimate criterion for a group head, but it's also the kind of vague, unmeasured attribute through which bias travels.

So: press for the written reasons and the scoring criteria first. Mention panel composition as background, never as your headline claim.
